title: Advanced Inference and Type Relationships knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to use a type or build feature?
options: Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
Assume compiler configuration has identical behavior in every version.
Use any whenever the types become difficult.
Treat type-level examples as proof of runtime correctness.
questions.answer_key: Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
questions.explanation: Type and build features must be evaluated in the actual configured project.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Advanced Inference and Type Relationships”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with contextual inference and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with contextual inference and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Contextual inference”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Advanced Inference and Type Relationships”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check preserving literal types, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume understanding inference failures is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check preserving literal types, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Preserving literal types”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
